description: Welcome to Team Feynman! I'm a Computer Systems Engineering student from Mexico, passionate about software development, science, and space exploration. I have experience with Angular, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, and REST APIs. Our goal is to build EarthScope, a web app that visualizes NASA Earth data. We're looking for teammates interested in coding, web development, data analysis, Earth science, and UI/UX design. Beginners are welcome!
summary:
EarthTrend NASA is an interactive Earth observation and climate analysis platform developed by Team Feynman for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project makes scientific climate data more accessible through an interactive 3D Earth explorer, global temperature visualizations, and historical climate analysis.

Using NASA POWER data, EarthTrend analyzes annual temperature observations, calculates statistical trends, and allows users to compare geographic locations and historical periods. NOAA atmospheric reanalysis data support the visualization of global temperature patterns.

Built with Angular 22, Three.js, TypeScript, Python, and FastAPI, the platform combines geospatial exploration with reproducible statistical analysis.

EarthTrend addresses the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" by helping users investigate environmental changes, identify measurable temperature trends, and understand scientific data through accessible visualizations.

Our goal is to promote climate awareness, scientific curiosity, and data literacy among students, educators, and the general public.
details:
EarthTrend NASA — Project Details

The Problem

Climate data are essential for understanding environmental changes, but scientific datasets can be difficult to access, visualize, and interpret without specialized knowledge.

Many people can observe temperature maps without understanding the difference between daily atmospheric conditions and long-term climate trends.

Our Solution

EarthTrend NASA is an interactive web platform that transforms scientific environmental data into accessible geographic visualizations and historical climate analysis.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our project helps users explore Earth, investigate temperature observations, and identify statistical trends.

How It Works

1. Interactive 3D Earth Explorer

Users explore a three-dimensional Earth developed with Three.js and WebGL. The globe supports rotation, zoom, geographic coordinate selection, and temperature visualization.

2. Global Temperature Visualization

EarthTrend uses NOAA NCEP–NCAR Reanalysis 1 data to display daily global temperature patterns through an interactive thermal layer.

3. Historical Climate Analysis

Users select geographic coordinates and a historical period. The Angular frontend communicates with a FastAPI backend that retrieves annual mean temperature observations from NASA POWER.

4. Statistical Trend Detection

The backend uses NumPy and SciPy to calculate annual mean temperature, minimum and maximum values, linear regression trends, R², and statistical significance.

Temperature trends are expressed in degrees Celsius per decade.

5. Geographic and Historical Comparisons

Users can compare two geographic locations or two historical periods using consistent analytical parameters.

6. Scientific Visualization and Export

Chart.js presents annual temperature observations and fitted trends. Users can export scientific data as CSV files and charts as PNG images.

Technologies Used

Frontend: Angular 22, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, WebGL, Chart.js, and RxJS.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, HTTPX, NumPy, SciPy, and xarray.

Scientific Data: NASA POWER and NOAA NCEP–NCAR Reanalysis 1.

Deployment: Vercel and Render.

Version Control: Git and GitHub.

Innovation

EarthTrend combines immersive geographic exploration with reproducible statistical analysis.

Instead of presenting isolated temperature maps, the platform connects geographic locations, historical observations, statistical trends, and scientific explanations in a unified experience.

The application distinguishes daily temperature patterns from historical climate trends and communicates important scientific limitations.

Intended Impact

EarthTrend aims to make Earth science more accessible to students, educators, developers, and the general public.

The project promotes scientific curiosity, climate awareness, and data literacy by making authentic environmental information easier to explore.

Scientific Integrity

EarthTrend uses scientific observations from NASA and NOAA.

Generative AI does not fabricate climate measurements.

The statistical analysis is descriptive and does not claim to establish climate causation or predict future temperatures.
